question.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+y-z=1 \\ x-2y+2z=3 \\ 3x-2y+z=2\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $5,$ then $x=$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system to reveal the coefficients:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+1y+(-1)z=1 \\ 1x+(-2)y+2z=3 \\ 3x+(-2)y+1z=2.\end{aligned}
$$

We start by writing the determinant of the coefficients matrix, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}|=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find ${D}_{x}$, we replace the first column by the right-hand side of the system, and calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x}=|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 \\ 3 & -2 & 2 \\ 2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2-(-4))-(3-4)-(-6-(-4)) \\  & =2+1+2 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying Cramer's rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{5}{5}=1.\end{aligned}
$$
